module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Coefficient of $(xyz)^n$ in $((x+y)(y+z)(z+x))^n$ equaling $\binom{2n}{n}^3$

The sequence $a(n)$ is defined by $a(n) = \binom{2n}{n}^3$.

*References:*
- [A002897](https://oeis.org/A002897)
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA2897


open Polynomial

open Nat MvPolynomial

/--
The sequence $a(n)$ is defined by $a(n) = \binom{2n}{n}^3$.
We use `Nat.choose (2 * n) n` for the central binomial coefficient.
-/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ := (Nat.choose (2 * n) n) ^ 3

abbrev Vars := Fin 3

/--
The finsupp corresponding to the monomial $x^n y^n z^n$.
This is the map $\lambda i. n$. Since `Fin 3` is finite, this function is finitely supported.
-/
noncomputable def xyzPowN (n : ℕ) : Finsupp Vars ℕ :=
  Finsupp.ofSupportFinite (fun _ : Vars => n) (Set.toFinite _)

local notation "P" => MvPolynomial Vars ℤ

/--
The polynomial $pPoly(X, Y, Z) = (1 + X + Y + Z)^{2n} (1 + X + Y - Z)^n (1 + X - Y + Z)^n$.
We identify $X_0, X_1, X_2$ with $X, Y, Z$.
-/
noncomputable def pPoly (n : ℕ) : P :=
  let X := MvPolynomial.X 0
  let Y := MvPolynomial.X 1
  let Z := MvPolynomial.X 2
  let p1 : P := 1 + X + Y + Z
  let p2 : P := 1 + X + Y - Z
  let p3 : P := 1 + X - Y + Z
  p1 ^ (2 * n) * p2 ^ n * p3 ^ n


@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_0 : a 0 = 1 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_1 : a 1 = 8 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_2 : a 2 = 216 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_3 : a 3 = 8000 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_4 : a 4 = 343000 := by rfl


/--
Conjecture: $a(n) = [x^n y^n z^n] (1+x+y+z)^{2n} (1+x+y-z)^n (1+x-y+z)^n$. - _Peter Bala_, Apr 10 2022

A formal proof has been found with the methods described in
[arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/a32396489dcb8f86c3549b93aa358ac6a10a3a1f/FormalConjectures/OEIS/2897.wip.lean#L408"]
theorem a_eq_coeff (n : ℕ) : (a n : ℤ) = MvPolynomial.coeff (xyzPowN n) (pPoly n) := by
    sorry

end OeisA2897

findings.description: The module heading at line 21 claims that the coefficient of (xyz)^n in ((x+y)(y+z)(z+x))^n equals binomial(2n,n)^3. This is a different, false identity: at n = 1 that coefficient is 2, whereas a(1) = 8. The definitions and OeisA2897.a_eq_coeff correctly use the polynomial from Bala's conjecture; only the heading is wrong. The n = 1 discrepancy was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without sorry or reliance on a_eq_coeff.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A002897, Peter Bala's Apr 10 2022 comment, gives a(n) = [(xyz)^n](1+x+y+z)^(2n)(1+x+y-z)^n(1+x-y+z)^n. Read through the official OEIS data mirror at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A002/A002897.seq. Easwar, arXiv:2608.22053, Corollary 4.5, states the same identity for n ≥ 0.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace ((x+y)(y+z)(z+x))^n in the module heading with (1+x+y+z)^(2n)(1+x+y-z)^n(1+x-y+z)^n, or use the title 'A binomial-cube coefficient identity (OEIS A002897)'. Leave the Lean declarations unchanged.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found in any Lean declaration. The sequence and all five tests agree with OEIS. The exponent vector has value n at each of the three variables, including the correct zero vector at n = 0. Scratch proofs verify the actual coefficients at n = 0 and 1; independent polynomial computations agree with the binomial cube for n = 0 through 6. OEIS explicitly records the coefficient identity as proved, so research solved is appropriate. The linked proof has the matching statement and no explicit sorry or custom axioms. A recompilation attempt against the current checkout encountered historical Mathlib API incompatibilities, so it did not independently kernel-verify that external proof; this is not evidence of a mathematical or status defect.
